title: $E$-coefficient smooth base change
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, let $A=\mathcal O_E$ and fix a uniformizer $\varpi$. Consider a cartesian square [sbc-def-base-change-square]
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
Y&\xrightarrow{h}&X\\
e\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
T&\xrightarrow{g}&S.
\end{array}
$$
Assume that $f$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], $g$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, all four schemes are noetherian, $X$ and $T$ have finite dimension, and $\ell$ is invertible on $S$. For each corner $W$, let $D_{\mathrm{comp}}(W,A)$ denote the full category of derived-complete complexes of modules over the completed coefficient sheaf $A_W$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum, def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion], and define
$$D_{\mathrm{comp}}(W,E)=D_{\mathrm{comp}}(W,A)[1/\varpi]$$
by raw scalar localization [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. For $W=X,T$, use $\Dbc(W,E)=\Dbc(W_{\mathrm{proet}},A)[1/\varpi]$ [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Rational completed pullback and direct image mean the scalar localizations of the corresponding integral completed functors [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]; their exchange is the scalar localization of the integral completed exchange.

Let $K_E\in\Dbc(T,E)$ admit a finite-level etale admissible lattice $L$ with a specified isomorphism $\iota:L[1/\varpi]\xrightarrow{\sim}K_E$ [sbc-def-admissible-lattices]. Then the exchange morphism is an isomorphism
$$
Lf^*_{\mathrm{comp},E}Rg_{*,\mathrm{comp},E}K_E
\xrightarrow{\sim}
Rh_{*,\mathrm{comp},E}Le^*_{\mathrm{comp},E}K_E
\quad\text{in }D_{\mathrm{comp}}(X,E).
$$
Its value at $K_E$, transported using $\iota$, is independent of the chosen admissible lattice and its presentation. If the lattice is square-constructibly admissible [sbc-def-admissible-lattices], this is an isomorphism in $\Dbc(X,E)$.

proof.text: The coefficient datum already contains finiteness and perfection of every positive quotient. The extended p-adic norm of l is less than one, so l lies in the maximal ideal generated by the chosen uniformizer, by lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr. Its (n+1)-st power therefore vanishes in the n-th quotient. The finite additive group of this quotient is an l-group, and Mathlib IsPGroup.exists_card_eq makes its cardinality a power of l. Mapping the given unit through the four global-section maps makes every quotient cardinality invertible on every corner. Mapping through global germs proves sbcPrimeUnitOnSource, including for an empty source.

source.place: Proof, opening two-term resolution; explicit arithmetic checks

proof.text: For every level, take the bounded constructible etale origin asserted by finite-level admissibility. Apply pbcDerivedFunctionRealization to its isomorphism and compose with the counit at the actual completed reduction. This supplies exactly the origin required by adicSmoothBaseChange for the given integral lattice; no origins are chosen as definition data.

Apply [sbc-thm-adic-smooth-base-change] to $L$. With $F=P_fD_g$ and $G=D_hP_e$, it gives the specified integral completed exchange $\alpha_L:F(L)\xrightarrow{\sim}G(L)$. Its source and target are complete complexes on $X$: $D_g$ first lands on $S$, $P_f$ then on $X$; $P_e$ first lands on $Y$, $D_h$ then on $X$. The assertion concerns the ambient complete categories and does not require $D_g(L)$ to be bounded constructible.

source.place: Proof, integral lattice exchange from the adic theorem

proof.text: Use [lem-sbc-completed-operations-linear-natural-exchange] for the four arrows, and the Hom-module construction of [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. For each integral functor $H$ define $H_E$ on objects by $H$ and on tensors by $H_E(a\otimes c)=H(a)\otimes c$. This is balanced because $H(ra)=rH(a)$, and additive in both variables, so it is well defined on the tensor product. On pure tensors, preservation of composition is $H(ba)\otimes dc=H(b)H(a)\otimes dc$, and identities map to identities; by bilinearity these identities hold on all morphisms. The same formulas show that localization commutes with the composites $F,G$. No constructibility preservation of arbitrary direct images is being used.

source.place: Proof, central localization; functor construction on Hom modules

proof.text:
Write $Q_W$ for the localization functor on the complete category at corner $W$. For every complete integral object $M$ (not only admissible lattices), define $\alpha_{E,Q_TM}=Q_X(\alpha_M)$. The naturality identity in [lem-sbc-completed-operations-linear-natural-exchange] tensor $c$ gives
$$G_E(a\otimes c)\,Q_X(\alpha_L)=Q_X(\alpha_{L'})\,F_E(a\otimes c).$$
Additivity proves naturality for every rational morphism, which is a finite sum of pure tensors. Thus these components form a transformation on the whole rationalized source. Its unit-square-counit formula is the integral formula with $Q$ applied: $Q$ preserves each composite, each inverse comparison, and the units and counits, whose triangle identities remain equalities. Therefore it is the specified rational exchange. From step 3, $Q_X(\alpha_L^{-1})$ is its inverse at the chosen lattice, since the two composites are $Q_X(1)=1$.

source.place: Proof, central localization of the specified exchange and its inverse

proof.text:
For any lattice presentation $i:Q_TL\xrightarrow{\sim}K_E$, the component on $K_E$ is
$$\beta_i=G_E(i)\,Q_X(\alpha_L)\,F_E(i)^{-1}.$$
For another presentation $i':Q_TL'\xrightarrow{\sim}K_E$, put $u=(i')^{-1}i$. The naturality proved in step 5 gives $Q_X(\alpha_{L'})F_E(u)=G_E(u)Q_X(\alpha_L)$. Substitute $i=i'u$ into the displayed expression and cancel $F_E(u)F_E(u)^{-1}$. The result is $\beta_i=G_E(i')Q_X(\alpha_{L'})F_E(i')^{-1}=\beta_{i'}$. This proves independence both of the lattice and of its specified identification with $K_E$. Notice that $u$ is a morphism in the raw rationalization [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]; no integral comparison of the lattices, common sublattice, or uniform bound on denominators on site objects is assumed.

source.place: Proof, independence of the admissible lattice; explicit conjugation identity

proof.text: Transfer the one common interval from square admissibility. Restrict function-ring modules along pbcLevelConstantComparison and then to fixed scalars. The associated-module sheafification unit, together with the coefficient scalar square, identifies this exact equivalence with the inverse of pbcFunctionRealization. Use the ordinary ring restriction-pullback comparison and pullbackEncoding to compare finite pullback with fixed upperStar. Use the ordinary direct-image comparison and directImageEncoding, then the exact/right-derived composition isomorphisms, to compare finite direct image with the right derived fixed lowerStar. The witness pullback and direct image have the same descriptions: simplify the realization equivalences and use finiteCoefficientRealization_directImage. Applying these comparisons to the reduction and successively to g, f, e and h identifies the four systems. Exactness identifies cohomology. The proved fixed_constructible_iff and coefficientConstructible_iff identify their intrinsic constructibility predicates, and full faithfulness reflects zero objects. Thus the identical interval is an input to the final clause of adicSmoothBaseChange. Take its two constructible integral endpoints, with identity inclusions into the ambient complete endpoints, and localize its isomorphism in the full subcategory. Its ambient map is the localized integral exchange by the pure tensor formula. Naturality along the specified lattice presentation is exactly the required representation equation.

source.place: Final clause: the four-system hypothesis gives constructible landing; integral landing from the final clause of sbc-thm-adic-smooth-base-change, followed by localization of the full subcategory.

proof_origin.place: Completed Lean proof: quotient l-group order, adic theorem, exact finite coefficient transport, localization and naturality. Source route and unit retained.

Its proof also claims coefficient-change compatibility not asserted by the E-coefficient theorem alone; that obligation must be audited in its own split.

old_proof.text:
The two-term free resolution
$[\mathcal O_E\xrightarrow{\varpi^{n+1}}\mathcal O_E]$ of $A_n$ and
the adic theorem [sbc-thm-adic-smooth-base-change] give the
statement for integral lattices; central localization (inverting
multiplication by $\varpi$) of
[def-weil-pbc-rational-category] gives
it for $K_E$, independent of the admissible lattice, and the
constructible landing is the four-system hypothesis of
[sbc-def-admissible-lattices].

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N6-48ff7ffad (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read every step of the item and the full statements of all 9 proof dependencies. I also read the main-20261015 blueprint statement and proof, plus the unit sk-thm-sbc-coefficients. The delivery creates no new nodes, and step uses match proof_deps exactly. The statement is unchanged; the inherited correction from S to X is right, tested on S=T=Spec k, X=Y=A^1_k. Step 1: from the DVR lemma and the finite-quotient leaf, A_n=A/ϖ^{n+1} has a two-term free resolution, ℓ=uϖ^r with r>0, and |A_n|=ℓ^{d(n+1)}, which is invertible on every corner. These are exactly the adic datum and adic-theorem hypotheses. Step 2: the finite-level étale admissibility of sbc-def-admissible-lattices matches the input of sbc-thm-adic-smooth-base-change word for word (same A_n indexing and same completed coefficient sheaf). Step 3 uses that theorem's statement only. Steps 4–5: the helper's linearity and naturality identity give G_E(a⊗c)Q(α_L)=Q(α_L')F_E(a⊗c), and the rational exchange is by definition Q of the helper's mate. Step 6: naturality at the presentation i, then the u=(i')^{-1}i cancellation, gives invertibility at K_E and independence of the lattice. Step 7: the four-system square-admissibility condition is exactly the hypothesis of the adic theorem's final clause. Since Dbc is a full subcategory, Q(α_L) is an isomorphism in Dbc(X,E), identified with the exchange through the endpoint identifications. This essential-image reading is the only meaningful one, matches the stage-2 Lean record, and does not weaken the statement. Edge cases checked: n=0, ramified E, the zero complex, the identity square, and non-integral rational re-presentations. The route follows the blueprint proof in order. Accepted tool_uses: lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr and lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients (the latter a Mathlib leaf), both used only to check coefficient hypotheses. No SGA source is cited. For the maintainer: the item's own tool_uses and reviewed fields are left over from the old nine-step split and still list nodes it no longer uses; the unit binding sk-rem-rest differs from main-20261015's sk-thm-sbc-coefficients; and the existing node def-pc-perfect-ring-complex cites Tag 0A1U where the definition is Tag 0657.
